newsitem.title: USA: Ohio Rep proposes excise tax hike for school bonds.
newsitem.headline: Ohio Rep proposes excise tax hike for school bonds.

text.p: Ohio state Rep. Gene Krebs, R-Camden, introduced legislation Thursday to eliminate state pricing controls on beer and wine and raise excise taxes on the products to generate revenue for school construction.
Krebs proposal to eliminate mandatory markups and minimum pricing for beer and wine in Ohio would generate $70 million in annual revenues, he said in a news release.
That revenue would then be used for a bond program that would generate more than $1 billion for school construction and improvements, Krebs said.
Even with an increase in the state excise tax, the elimination of the markups and pricing requirements would result in a 2 percent reduction in beer and wine prices, Krebs said.
Under the proposal, the excise tax on a six-pack of beer would rise from 8 cents to 26 cents and on a 750 ml bottle of wine from 5 cents to 20 cents.
Krebs' bill would also reduce the inventory tax rate from 25 percent to 20 percent, with the eventual goal of eliminating it. Ohio is one of a handful of states that continues to tax inventory.
